title.zh: 卷十七 晉家人傳第五:
title.en: Volume 17: The Later Jin Imperial Family
title.raw: 卷十七 晉家人傳第五: Volume 17: The Later Jin Imperial Family

sentences.zh: 高祖皇后李氏

translations.literal: Empress Li, Consort of Gaozu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li, Consort of Gaozu

sentences.zh: 高祖皇后李氏，唐明宗皇帝女也。

translations.literal: Empress Li, consort of Gaozu, was a daughter of Emperor Mingzong of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Li, Gaozu’s consort, was a daughter of Tang’s Emperor Mingzong.

sentences.zh: 后初號永寧公主，清泰二年封魏國長公主。

translations.literal: She was first titled Princess Yongning; in the second year of Qingtai she was enfeoffed Grand Princess of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: She was first styled Princess Yongning; in Qingtai 2 she was made Grand Princess of Wei.

sentences.zh: 自廢帝立，常疑高祖必反。

translations.literal: From the time the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he often suspected Gaozu would rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Deposed Emperor rose, he constantly feared Gaozu would rebel.

sentences.zh: 三年，公主自太原入朝千春節，辭歸，留之不得，廢帝醉，語公主曰：「爾歸何速，欲與石郎反邪？

translations.literal: In the third year the princess came from Taiyuan to court for the Qianchun Festival; when she took leave to return they could not detain her. The Deposed Emperor, drunk, said to the princess: “Why return so soon—do you mean to rebel with that fellow Shi?
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the princess came from Taiyuan for the Qianchun Festival; when she asked leave to go home they could not hold her. The Deposed Emperor, drunk, told the princess: “Why leave so fast—do you plan to rebel with that Shi fellow?

sentences.zh: 」既醒，左右告之，廢帝大悔。

translations.literal: ” When he sobered, those around him told him, and the Deposed Emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: ” When he woke, his attendants told him what he had said, and the Deposed Emperor was filled with remorse.

sentences.zh: 公主歸，以語高祖，高祖由是益不自安。

translations.literal: The princess returned and told Gaozu; Gaozu was therefore all the more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: The princess went home and told Gaozu; from then on he felt still less secure.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，公主當為皇后。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, the princess was to become empress.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu succeeded, the princess was to be made empress.

sentences.zh: 天福二年三月，有司言：「皇太妃尊號已正，請上寶冊。

translations.literal: In the third month of Tianfu 2 the responsible officials said: “The Grand Consort’s honorific title has been set—we ask to present the imperial seal and patent.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianfu 2 the court said: “The Grand Consort’s title is now settled—we beg to invest her with seal and patent.

sentences.zh: 」太妃，高祖庶母劉氏也。

translations.literal: ” The Grand Consort was Liu, Gaozu’s stepmother.
translations.idiomatic: ” The Grand Consort was Liu, Gaozu’s stepmother.

sentences.zh: 高祖以宗廟未立，謙抑未皇。

translations.literal: Gaozu, since the ancestral temple had not yet been established, was modest and held back.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, the ancestral temple not yet built, was humble and deferred.

sentences.zh: 七年夏五月，高祖已病，乃詔尊太妃為皇太后，然卒不奉冊而高祖崩，故后訖高祖世亦無冊命。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer, Tianfu 7, Gaozu already ill, issued an edict honoring the Grand Consort as empress dowager; yet the patent was never delivered before he died, so the empress too received no formal investiture throughout Gaozu’s reign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer, Tianfu 7, Gaozu, already failing, decreed the Grand Consort empress dowager—but died before the patent could be given, and the empress received no investiture at all in Gaozu’s lifetime.

sentences.zh: 出帝天福八年七月，冊尊皇后為皇太后。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of Tianfu 8 under Emperor Chu, the empress was formally invested as empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianfu 8, under Emperor Chu, the empress was invested as empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 太后為人強敏，高祖常嚴憚之。

translations.literal: The dowager was forceful and shrewd; Gaozu often stood in awe of her.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager was sharp and resolute; Gaozu often feared her.

sentences.zh: 出帝馮皇后用事，太后數訓戒之，出帝不從，乃及於敗。

translations.literal: Emperor Chu’s wife Empress Feng held power; the dowager repeatedly admonished her, but Emperor Chu would not listen—and thus came ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Feng, Emperor Chu’s consort, ran affairs; the dowager warned her again and again, but Emperor Chu would not heed her—and ruin followed.

sentences.zh: 開運三年十二月，耶律德光已降晉兵，遣張彥澤先犯京師，以書遺太后，具道已降晉軍，且曰：「吾有梳頭妮子竊一藥囊以奔於晉，今皆在否？

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Kaiyun 3 Yelü Deguang had already received the surrender of Jin troops and sent Zhang Yanze ahead to strike the capital; he sent a letter to the dowager detailing the surrendered Jin army, and said: “I had a comb-girl who stole a medicine pouch and fled to Jin—are they all still there?
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Kaiyun 3 Yelü Deguang had already taken the surrender of the Jin armies and sent Zhang Yanze ahead against the capital; he wrote the dowager, setting out how the Jin had submitted, and asked: “I had a girl who combed my hair—she stole a medicine pouch and ran off to Jin. Are they all still there?

sentences.zh: 吾戰陽城時，亡奚車一乘，在否？

translations.literal: When I fought at Yangcheng I lost one Xi cart—is it still there?
translations.idiomatic: When I fought at Yangcheng I lost a Xi carriage—is it still there?

sentences.zh: 」又問契丹先為晉獲者及景延廣、桑維翰等所在。

translations.literal: ” He also asked where those Khitan previously captured by Jin were, and where Jing Yanguang, Sang Weihan, and others were.
translations.idiomatic: ” He also asked after Khitan taken earlier by Jin, and where Jing Yanguang, Sang Weihan, and the rest might be.

sentences.zh: 太后與帝聞彥澤至，欲自焚，嬖臣薛超勸止之。

translations.literal: The dowager and the emperor, hearing Yanze had arrived, meant to burn themselves; the favorite minister Xue Chao urged them to stop.
translations.idiomatic: When the dowager and the emperor heard Yanze was coming, they prepared to die by fire; the favorite Xue Chao persuaded them to hold back.

sentences.zh: 及得德光所與書，乃滅火，出上苑中。

translations.literal: When they received Deguang’s letter, they extinguished the fire and went out into the upper garden.
translations.idiomatic: Once Deguang’s letter arrived, they put out the flames and went out into the upper garden.

sentences.zh: 帝召當直學士範質，謂曰：「杜郎一何相負！

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the duty academician Fan Zhi and said: “How could Du have betrayed us so!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called the duty academician Fan Zhi and said: “How Du has failed us!

sentences.zh: 昔先帝起太原時，欲擇一子留守，謀之北朝皇帝，皇帝以屬我，我素以為其所知，卿為我草奏具言之，庶幾活我子母。

translations.literal: When my late father rose at Taiyuan, he wished to choose a son to remain behind and consulted the Khitan emperor; the emperor entrusted the matter to me—I always believed he knew this. Draft a memorial for me setting out all of this in full, so perhaps my mother and I may yet live.
translations.idiomatic: When my late father first raised the banner at Taiyuan, he meant to leave one son behind and asked the Khitan emperor’s counsel; the emperor chose me—I always thought he understood. Draft a memorial for me and tell the whole story plainly; perhaps it will save my mother and me.

sentences.zh: 」質為帝草降表曰：

translations.literal: ” Fan Zhi drafted a surrender memorial for the emperor:
translations.idiomatic: ” Fan Zhi drafted a surrender memorial for the emperor:

sentences.zh: 孫男臣重貴言：頃者唐運告終，中原失馭，數窮否極，天缺地傾。

translations.literal: Your Majesty’s grandson and subject Chonggui speaks: Not long ago the mandate of Tang expired, the Central Plains lost their ruler, fortune ran to its end and misfortune reached its extreme—Heaven cracked and Earth tilted.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty’s grandson and subject Chonggui speaks: Lately the Tang mandate ended, the Central Plains lost their guide, number and fortune were spent and ruin complete—Heaven gaped and Earth gave way.

sentences.zh: 先人有田一成，有眾一旅，兵連禍結，力屈勢孤。

translations.literal: My forebear held one patch of land and one company of men; war bred calamity after calamity until his strength was broken and he stood alone.
translations.idiomatic: My forebear held one field and one band of men; battle piled on disaster until his strength failed and he stood alone.

sentences.zh: 翁皇帝救患摧剛，興利除害，躬擐甲胃，深入寇場。

translations.literal: Honored Imperial Father, you crushed misfortune and broke stubborn foes, you raised up good and swept away harm, yourself bearing armor and plunged deep into the field of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Imperial Father, you rescued the afflicted and broke the hard-hearted, brought profit and cleared away harm, yourself donning armor and driving deep into the enemy’s ground.

sentences.zh: 犯露蒙霜，度雁門之險；

translations.literal: You braved dew and frost, crossed the peril of Yanmen Pass;
translations.idiomatic: You faced dew and frost and crossed the danger of Yanmen Pass;

sentences.zh: 馳風擊電，行中冀之誅。

translations.literal: like wind and lightning you raced to execute judgment in central Ji.
translations.idiomatic: like wind and thunder you struck to punish the heart of Ji.

sentences.zh: 黃鉞一麾，天下大定，勢淩宇宙，義感神明。

translations.literal: At one wave of the golden battle-axe the realm was pacified; your power towered over Heaven and Earth, your righteousness moved the gods.
translations.idiomatic: One sweep of the yellow axe and the realm was settled; your might rose above Heaven and Earth, your righteousness touched the spirits.

sentences.zh: 功成不居，遂興晉祚，則翁皇帝有大造於石氏也。

translations.literal: Having achieved success you did not keep it for yourself but raised the Jin dynasty—thus the Honored Imperial Father wrought great creation for the House of Shi.
translations.idiomatic: You took no reward for victory but raised the Jin throne—thus the Honored Imperial Father gave the House of Shi a new life.

sentences.zh: 旋屬天降鞠兇，先君即世，臣遵承遺旨，篡紹前基。

translations.literal: Soon Heaven sent down calamity and my late father passed; I followed his dying command and seized his place to succeed the former foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Then Heaven sent down grief and my late father died; I obeyed his last charge and usurped the line to carry on what he had built.

sentences.zh: 諒闇之初，荒迷失次，凡有軍國重事，皆委將相大臣。

translations.literal: In the first days of mourning I was lost and out of order; all weighty matters of state and army I entrusted to my generals and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of my mourning I was dazed and without bearing; every grave matter of army and state I left to my generals and ministers.

sentences.zh: 至於擅繼宗祧，既非廩命；

translations.literal: Yet to seize the ancestral line of my own accord was never Heaven’s appointed decree;
translations.idiomatic: Yet to take the ancestral succession on my own was no mandate from Heaven;

sentences.zh: 輕發文字，輒敢抗尊。

translations.literal: I lightly issued writs and repeatedly dared to resist Your Majesty’s supreme authority.
translations.idiomatic: I sent out words too lightly and again and again resisted Your Majesty’s supreme will.

sentences.zh: 自啟釁端，果貽赫怒，禍至神惑，運盡天亡。

translations.literal: I opened the quarrel myself and truly earned your thunderous wrath; calamity came, the spirits were confounded, my fortune was spent and Heaven decreed my end.
translations.idiomatic: I began the breach myself and brought down your thunder; disaster arrived, the gods were troubled, my luck ran out and Heaven pronounced my fall.

sentences.zh: 十萬師徒，望風束手；

translations.literal: A hundred thousand soldiers stood with arms bound at the mere rumor of your approach;
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand troops waited with bound hands at the wind of your coming;

sentences.zh: 億兆黎庶，延頸歸心。

translations.literal: millions upon millions of common people craned their necks and turned their hearts to you.
translations.idiomatic: millions of common people stretched their necks and gave you their hearts.

sentences.zh: 臣負義包羞，貪生忍恥，自貽顛覆，上累祖宗，偷度朝昏，茍存視息。

translations.literal: I bear guilt and wrap myself in shame, clinging to life and enduring disgrace, bringing on my own overthrow and heaping shame upon my ancestors; I steal through each day and night, barely keeping breath in my body.
translations.idiomatic: I am guilty and shamed, greedy for life and swallowing humiliation, overthrowing myself and burdening my ancestors; I crawl through each dawn and dusk, barely drawing breath.

sentences.zh: 翁皇帝若惠顧疇昔，稍霽雷霆，未賜靈誅，不絕先祀，則百口荷更生之德，一門銜無報之恩，雖所願焉，非敢望也。

translations.literal: Honored Imperial Father, if you would look back upon old ties, let your thunder roll back a little, withhold the punishing blade, and do not cut off our ancestral sacrifices—then our hundred mouths would receive the grace of renewed life and our whole house would hold an unpayable debt of gratitude. That is our humble wish, though we dare not expect it.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Imperial Father, if you would remember old kindness and soften your thunder, withhold the stroke of punishment, and not sever our ancestral rites, then our hundred mouths would owe the debt of rebirth and our whole house would carry a gratitude beyond repayment. That is our wish, though we dare not hope for it.

sentences.zh: 臣與太后、妻馮氏於郊野面縛俟罪次。

translations.literal: I, together with the Empress Dowager and my wife Lady Feng, await judgment in the open country with bound hands and faces.
translations.idiomatic: I, with the Empress Dowager and my wife Lady Feng, wait in the open fields with faces and hands bound for judgment.

sentences.zh: 又為太后表曰：

translations.literal: Another memorial was drafted for the Empress Dowager:
translations.idiomatic: Another memorial was drafted for the Empress Dowager:

sentences.zh: 晉室皇太后新婦李氏妾言：張彥澤、傅住兒等至，伏蒙皇帝阿翁降書安撫者。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager of the Jin house, new wife and subject Li, speaks: Zhang Yanze, Fu Zhuer, and others have arrived; we humbly received the comforting letter from the Emperor Honored Father-in-Law.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager of Jin, new wife and subject Li, speaks: Zhang Yanze, Fu Zhuer, and others have come; we humbly received the reassuring letter from the Emperor Honored Father-in-Law.

sentences.zh: 妾伏念先皇帝頃在並、汾，適逢屯難，危同累卵，急若倒懸，智勇俱窮，朝夕不保。

translations.literal: I recall that my late husband the emperor, when he was in Bing and Fen, met sudden peril; danger piled like eggs in a stack, urgency hung like an inverted cleaver; wit and courage alike were exhausted and each day and night hung by a thread.
translations.idiomatic: I remember when my late husband was at Bing and Fen, sudden hardship fell; danger stacked like eggs, urgency like a man hung upside down; wit and courage were spent and each day and night held no promise.

sentences.zh: 皇帝阿翁發自冀北，親抵河東，跋履山川，逾越險阻。

translations.literal: The Emperor Honored Father-in-Law marched from north of Ji, came in person to Hedong, crossed mountains and rivers, surmounted every barrier.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Honored Father-in-Law set out from north of Ji, came himself to Hedong, tramped over mountains and rivers, and crossed every peril.

sentences.zh: 立平巨孽，遂定中原，救石氏之覆亡，立晉朝之社稷。

translations.literal: He swiftly crushed the great evil and settled the Central Plains, saving the House of Shi from destruction and establishing the altars of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He quickly put down the great scourge and settled the Central Plains, saving the House of Shi from ruin and raising the altars of Jin.

sentences.zh: 不幸先帝厭代，嗣子承祧，不能繼好息民，而反虧恩辜義。

translations.literal: Alas, my late husband passed from this world; the heir took up the ancestral line but could not continue friendship and give the people peace—instead he betrayed kindness and broke faith.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my late husband died; the heir took the ancestral line but could not keep peace and renew friendship—instead he wronged kindness and broke faith.

sentences.zh: 兵戈屢動，駟馬難追，戚實自貽，咎將誰執！

translations.literal: Wars rose again and again; four-horse chariots could not overtake what was done—grief was truly self-wrought; on whom else can blame fall?
translations.idiomatic: Arms moved again and again; even four horses could not chase back what was done—sorrow was truly self-made; on whom else can blame be laid?

sentences.zh: 今穹旻震怒，中外攜離，上將牽羊，六師解甲。

translations.literal: Now Heaven’s vault thunders in wrath; within and without all have turned away; the lords bring sheep in submission and the six armies lay down their arms.
translations.idiomatic: Now Heaven rages; within and without all have parted; the lords come leading sheep and the six armies cast off their armor.

sentences.zh: 妾舉宗負釁，視景偷生，惶惑之中，撫問斯至，明宣恩旨，典示含容，慰諭丁寧，神爽飛越。

translations.literal: I and my whole clan bear guilt; we clung to life at the sight of the sun. In our bewilderment your inquiry arrived; your gracious intent was proclaimed, your tolerant decree displayed, your soothing words repeated—and our spirits soared.
translations.idiomatic: I and my whole house bear fault; we clung to life while we could. In our confusion your inquiry came; your gracious will was declared, your tolerant example shown, your comforting words repeated—and our spirits lifted.

sentences.zh: 豈謂已垂之命，忽蒙更生之恩，省罪責躬，九死未報。

translations.literal: Who would have thought that lives already forfeit should suddenly receive the mercy of rebirth? We examine our sins and blame ourselves; even nine deaths could not repay this grace.
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought lives already forfeit would suddenly receive the gift of life again? We review our crimes and blame ourselves; nine deaths would not repay this mercy.

sentences.zh: 今遣孫男延煦、延寶，奉表請罪，陳謝以聞。

translations.literal: Now I send my grandsons Yanxu and Yanbao to present this memorial begging pardon, that our repentance may be heard.
translations.idiomatic: Now I send my grandsons Yanxu and Yanbao with this memorial to beg forgiveness and report our shame.

sentences.zh: 德光報曰：「可無憂，管取一吃飯處。」

translations.literal: Deguang replied: “You need not worry—I will find you somewhere to eat.”
translations.idiomatic: Deguang answered: “Do not worry—I’ll see you get a place to eat.”

sentences.zh: 四年正月丁亥朔，德光入京師，帝與太后肩輿至郊外，德光不見，館於封禪寺，遣其將崔延勛以兵守之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the first day of the first month of the fourth year, Deguang entered the capital. The emperor and the dowager came in palanquins to the suburbs; Deguang would not receive them and lodged them at Fengchan Temple, sending his general Cui Yanxun with troops to guard them.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the first day of the first month of the fourth year, Deguang entered the capital. The emperor and the dowager came in palanquins to the outskirts; Deguang would not see them and housed them at Fengchan Temple, posting his general Cui Yanxun with soldiers to keep watch.

sentences.zh: 是時雨雪寒凍，皆苦饑。

translations.literal: At that time snow and rain fell and the cold was bitter; all suffered hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Snow and icy rain fell then; hunger tormented them all.

sentences.zh: 太后使人謂寺僧曰：「吾嘗於此飯僧數萬，今日豈不相憫邪？

translations.literal: The dowager sent word to the temple monks: “I once fed tens of thousands of monks here—will you not pity us today?
translations.idiomatic: The dowager sent word to the temple monks: “I once fed tens of thousands of monks here—will you not show mercy today?

sentences.zh: 」寺僧辭以虜意難測，不敢獻食。

translations.literal: ” The monks pleaded that the barbarians’ intent was hard to read and dared not offer food.
translations.idiomatic: ” The monks answered that the invaders’ mood was unknowable and they dared not bring food.

sentences.zh: 帝陰祈守者，乃稍得食。

translations.literal: The emperor secretly pleaded with the guards and thus obtained a little food.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor quietly begged the guards and so received a little food.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，德光降帝為光祿大夫、檢校太尉，封「負義侯」，遷於黃龍府。

translations.literal: On xinmao Deguang demoted the emperor to Grand Counselor of the Imperial Insignia, acting Grand General, with the title “Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness,” and moved him to Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Deguang reduced the emperor to Grand Counselor of the Imperial Insignia and acting Grand General, enfeoffed him “Marquis Who Betrayed Righteousness,” and sent him to Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 德光使人謂太后曰：「吾聞重貴不從母教而至於此，可求自便，勿與俱行。

translations.literal: Deguang sent word to the dowager: “I hear Chonggui would not obey his mother’s teaching and came to this—seek your own convenience; do not travel with him.
translations.idiomatic: Deguang sent word to the dowager: “I hear Chonggui ignored his mother’s counsel and brought this on himself—take your own ease; do not go with him.

sentences.zh: 」太后答曰：「重貴事妾甚謹。

translations.literal: ” The dowager answered: “Chonggui served me with great care.
translations.idiomatic: ” The dowager replied: “Chonggui served me faithfully.

sentences.zh: 所失者，違先君之志，絕兩國之歡。

translations.literal: What failed was that he went against our late lord’s will and broke friendship between the two realms.
translations.idiomatic: What failed was that he betrayed our late lord’s intent and severed friendship between our two states.

sentences.zh: 然重貴此去，幸蒙大惠，全生保家，母不隨子，欲何所歸！

translations.literal: Yet if Chonggui goes now and receives great mercy, with life preserved and house intact, how could a mother not follow her son—where would I go?
translations.idiomatic: Yet if Chonggui goes now under great mercy, with life and house spared, how could a mother leave her son—where would I turn?

sentences.zh: 」於是太后與馮皇后、皇弟重睿、皇子延煦、延寶等舉族從帝而北，以宮女五十、宦者三十、東西班五十、醫官一、控鶴官四、禦廚七、茶酒司三、儀鸞司三、六軍士二十人從，衛以騎兵三百。

translations.literal: So the dowager, with Empress Feng, the emperor’s younger brother Chongrui, and the princes Yanxu and Yanbao, went north with the whole clan; fifty palace women, thirty eunuchs, fifty eastern and western attendants, one medical officer, four Crane-Taming officers, seven imperial kitchen staff, three tea-and-wine offices, three ceremonial-bird offices, and twenty soldiers of the Six Armies followed, guarded by three hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: So the dowager, Empress Feng, the emperor’s younger brother Chongrui, and the princes Yanxu and Yanbao went north with the whole clan—fifty palace women, thirty eunuchs, fifty eastern and western attendants, one physician, four Crane-Taming officers, seven imperial cooks, three tea-and-wine offices, three ceremonial offices, and twenty soldiers of the Six Armies in attendance, escorted by three hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 所經州縣，皆故晉將吏，有所供饋，不得通。

translations.literal: Every prefecture and county they passed was held by former Jin officers and men, yet no supplies could reach them.
translations.idiomatic: Every prefecture and county they passed was manned by former Jin officers, yet nothing could get through to them.

sentences.zh: 路傍父老，爭持羊酒為獻，衛兵推隔不使見帝，皆涕泣而去。

translations.literal: Old men by the road pressed forward with sheep and wine as gifts; the guards pushed them back and would not let them see the emperor, and all wept as they left.
translations.idiomatic: Elders along the road pressed forward with sheep and wine; the guards held them off and kept them from the emperor, and all went away weeping.

sentences.zh: 自幽州行十餘日，過平州，出榆關，行砂磧中，饑不得食，遣宮女、從官，采木實、野蔬而食。

translations.literal: After more than ten days from Youzhou, passing Pingzhou and out through Yugu Pass, they traveled through sandy desert, starving without food; palace women and attendants gathered tree fruit and wild greens to eat.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten days out from Youzhou, through Pingzhou and Yugu Pass, they crossed sandy wastes, starving for food; palace women and attendants gathered tree fruit and wild herbs to eat.

sentences.zh: 又行七八日，至錦州，虜人迫帝與太后拜阿保機畫像。

translations.literal: After another seven or eight days they reached Jin Prefecture; the barbarians forced the emperor and the dowager to bow before Abaoji’s portrait.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight days later they reached Jin Prefecture; the Khitan forced the emperor and the dowager to bow before Abaoji’s portrait.

sentences.zh: 帝不勝其辱，泣而呼曰：「薛超誤我，不令我死！

translations.literal: The emperor could not bear the humiliation and wept, crying: “Xue Chao misled me—he would not let me die!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not bear the shame and wept, crying: “Xue Chao misled me—he would not let me die!

sentences.zh: 」又行五六日，過海北州，至東丹王墓，遣延煦拜之。

translations.literal: ” After another five or six days they passed Haibei Prefecture, reached the tomb of the Prince of Dongdan, and sent Yanxu to pay respects.
translations.idiomatic: ” Five or six days later they passed Haibei Prefecture, came to the Prince of Dongdan’s tomb, and sent Yanxu to bow there.

sentences.zh: 又行十餘日，渡遼水，至渤海國鐵州。

translations.literal: After another ten-odd days they crossed the Liao River and reached Tied Prefecture in the Bohai state.
translations.idiomatic: Ten-odd days later they crossed the Liao River and reached Tied Prefecture in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 又行七八日，過南海府，遂至黃龍府。

translations.literal: After another seven or eight days they passed Nanhai Prefecture and at last reached Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Seven or eight days later they passed Nanhai Prefecture and finally reached Huanglong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲六月，契丹國母徙帝、太后於懷密州，州去黃龍府西北一千五百里。

translations.literal: That year in the sixth month the Khitan empress dowager moved the emperor and the dowager to Huaimi Prefecture, fifteen hundred li northwest of Huanglong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That sixth month the Khitan empress dowager moved the emperor and the dowager to Huaimi Prefecture, fifteen hundred li northwest of Huanglong.

sentences.zh: 行過遼陽二百里，而國母為永康王所囚，永康王遣帝、太后還止遼陽，稍供給之。

translations.literal: Two hundred li past Liaoyang the empress dowager was imprisoned by Prince Yongkang; Prince Yongkang sent the emperor and the dowager back to halt at Liaoyang and gave them a little supply.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred li beyond Liaoyang the Khitan empress dowager was seized by Prince Yongkang; he sent the emperor and the dowager back to stay at Liaoyang and gave them some provisions.

sentences.zh: 明年四月，永康王至遼陽，帝白衣紗帽，與太后、皇后詣帳中上謁，永康王止帝以常服見。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the next year Prince Yongkang came to Liaoyang; the emperor in white cloth and gauze cap, with the dowager and the empress, went to his tent to pay homage; Prince Yongkang had the emperor received in ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: The next fourth month Prince Yongkang came to Liaoyang; the emperor in white cloth and gauze cap, with the dowager and empress, went to his tent to pay court; Prince Yongkang had him received in plain clothes.

sentences.zh: 帝伏地雨泣，自陳過咎。

translations.literal: The emperor prostrated himself and wept like rain, confessing his faults.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor fell to the ground weeping and confessed his crimes.

sentences.zh: 永康王使人扶起之，與坐，飲酒奏樂。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang had men raise him up and sat with him, drinking wine while music played.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang had men lift him up and sat with him, drinking and listening to music.

sentences.zh: 而永康王帳下伶人、從官，望見故主，皆泣下，悲不自勝，爭以衣服藥餌為遺。

translations.literal: Yet the actors and attendants in Prince Yongkang’s camp, seeing their former lord, all wept until they could not bear it and vied to give him clothes, medicine, and food.
translations.idiomatic: Actors and attendants in Prince Yongkang’s camp, seeing their old master, wept until they could not stand it and pressed clothes, medicine, and food on him.

sentences.zh: 五月，永康王上陘，取帝所從行宦者十五人、東西班十五人及皇子延煦而去。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Prince Yongkang went up to the heights and took fifteen eunuchs from the emperor’s retinue, fifteen eastern and western attendants, and the prince Yanxu with him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Prince Yongkang went up to the heights and took fifteen of the emperor’s eunuchs, fifteen eastern and western attendants, and Prince Yanxu with him.

sentences.zh: 永康王妻兄禪奴愛帝小女，求之，帝辭以尚幼。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang’s brother-in-law Chanu loved the emperor’s younger daughter and asked for her; the emperor refused, saying she was still too young.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang’s brother-in-law Chanu wanted the emperor’s younger daughter and asked for her; the emperor refused, saying she was still young.

sentences.zh: 永康王馳一騎取之，以賜禪奴。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang galloped off on one horse, took her, and gave her to Chanu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang rode off alone, seized her, and gave her to Chanu.

sentences.zh: 陘，虜地，尤高涼，虜人常以五月上陘避暑，八月下陘。

translations.literal: The heights were Khitan territory, especially cool and high; the Khitan commonly went up in the fifth month to escape the heat and came down in the eighth month.
translations.idiomatic: The heights were Khitan land, cool and lofty; the Khitan usually went up in the fifth month to escape the heat and came down in the eighth.

sentences.zh: 至八月，永康王下陘，太后自馳至霸州見永康王，求於漢兒城側賜地種牧以為生。

translations.literal: When the eighth month came and Prince Yongkang came down from the heights, the dowager rode in haste to Bazhou to see him and begged for land beside Hanyang City to farm and herd for a living.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, when Prince Yongkang came down from the heights, the dowager rode hard to Bazhou to see him and begged for land near Hanyang City to farm and herd and live by.

sentences.zh: 永康王以太后自從，行十餘日，遣與延煦俱還遼陽。

translations.literal: Prince Yongkang, since the dowager had come with him, after more than ten days sent her back with Yanxu to Liaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yongkang, the dowager having come with him, after ten-odd days sent her back with Yanxu to Liaoyang.

sentences.zh: 明年乃漢乾祐二年，其二月，徙帝、太后於建州。

translations.literal: The next year was the second year of Qianyou of Han; in the second month the emperor and the dowager were moved to Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year was Han Qianyou 2; in the second month the emperor and the dowager were moved to Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自遼陽東南行千二百里至建州，節度使趙延暉避正寢以館之。

translations.literal: From Liaoyang they traveled southeast twelve hundred li to Jian Prefecture; Military Governor Zhao Yanhui vacated his main quarters to lodge them.
translations.idiomatic: From Liaoyang they went southeast twelve hundred li to Jian Prefecture; Military Governor Zhao Yanhui gave up his own main hall to house them.

sentences.zh: 去建州數十里外得地五十餘頃，帝遣從行者耕而食之。

translations.literal: Several tens of li outside Jian Prefecture they received more than fifty qing of land; the emperor had those who followed him farm it for food.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of li from Jian Prefecture they were given more than fifty qing of land; the emperor had his followers farm it to eat.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，太后寢疾，無醫藥，常仰天而泣，南望戟手罵杜重威、李守貞等曰：「使死者無知則已，若其有知，不赦爾於地下！

translations.literal: In the third month of the next year the dowager fell ill; without medicine or doctors she often wept to Heaven, and facing south shook her fist at Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and the rest, saying: “If the dead know nothing, so be it; if they know, may they not forgive you in the underworld!
translations.idiomatic: The next third month the dowager sickened; without medicine or physicians she often wept to Heaven, and facing south shook her fist at Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, and the rest, saying: “If the dead know nothing, so be it; if they know, may they never pardon you beneath the earth!

sentences.zh: 」八月疾亟，謂帝曰：「我死，焚其骨送范陽佛寺，無使我為虜地鬼也！

translations.literal: ” In the eighth month, gravely ill, she told the emperor: “When I die, burn my bones and send them to a Fan Yang Buddhist temple—do not let me become a ghost in barbarian land!
translations.idiomatic: ” In the eighth month, near death, she told the emperor: “When I die, burn my bones and send them to a Fan Yang temple—do not let me be a ghost in barbarian soil!

sentences.zh: 」遂卒。

translations.literal: ” And she died.
translations.idiomatic: ” Then she died.

sentences.zh: 帝與皇后、宮人、宦者、東西班，皆被髮徙跣，扶舁其柩至賜地，焚其骨，穿地而葬焉。

translations.literal: The emperor, with the empress, palace women, eunuchs, and eastern and western attendants, all tore their hair and went barefoot, carrying the bier to the allotted land, burning the bones and burying them in a pit dug in the earth.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, with the empress, palace women, eunuchs, and eastern and western attendants, all let down their hair and went barefoot, carrying the coffin to the allotted land, burning the bones and burying them in a pit.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，有中國人自契丹亡歸者，言見帝與皇后諸子皆無恙。

translations.literal: During the Xiande reign of Zhou, a Chinese who escaped from the Khitan said he had seen the emperor and the empress with their sons—all unharmed.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Zhou’s Xiande era a Chinese who fled the Khitan said he had seen the emperor and empress with their sons—all still alive.

sentences.zh: 後不知其所終。

translations.literal: Afterward their end was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: After that no one knew their fate.

sentences.zh: 太妃安氏

translations.literal: Grand Consort An
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort An

sentences.zh: 安太妃，代北人也，不知其世家，為敬儒妻，生出帝，封秦國夫人。

translations.literal: Grand Consort An was a woman of northern Dai; her family is unknown. She was the wife of Jing Ru, bore Emperor Chu, and was enfeoffed Lady of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Consort An came from northern Dai; her lineage is unknown. Wife of Jing Ru, she bore Emperor Chu and was made Lady of Qin.

sentences.zh: 出帝立，尊為皇太妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Chu took the throne, she was honored as imperial grand consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Chu succeeded, she was honored as imperial grand consort.

sentences.zh: 妃老而失明，從出帝北遷，自遼陽徙建州，卒於道中。

translations.literal: Old and blind, she followed Emperor Chu north; from Liaoyang she was moved to Jian Prefecture and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Old and blind, she followed Emperor Chu north; from Liaoyang she was moved toward Jian Prefecture and died on the way.

sentences.zh: 臨卒謂帝曰：「當焚我為灰，南向揚之，庶幾遺魂得反中國也。

translations.literal: Near death she told the emperor: “Burn me to ash and scatter it facing south, so perhaps my lingering soul may return to China.
translations.idiomatic: Near death she told the emperor: “Burn me to ash and scatter it toward the south, so perhaps my wandering soul may reach China again.

sentences.zh: 」既卒，砂磧中無草木，乃毀奚車而焚之，載其燼骨至建州。

translations.literal: ” After she died, with no wood or grass in the sandy wastes, they broke up a Xi cart to burn her and carried the ashes to Jian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: ” When she died there was no wood or grass in the sandy wastes, so they broke up a Xi cart to burn her and carried the ashes on to Jian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李太后亦卒，遂並葬之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Li had also died, and they were buried together.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Li had died as well, and they were buried together.

sentences.zh: 出帝皇后馮氏

translations.literal: Empress Feng, Consort of Emperor Chu
translations.idiomatic: Empress Feng, Consort of Emperor Chu

sentences.zh: 出帝皇后馮氏，定州人也。

translations.literal: Empress Feng of the Fleeing Emperor was a native of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Feng, consort of the Fleeing Emperor, came from Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父濛，為州進奏吏，居京師，以巧佞為安重誨所喜，以為鄴都副留守。

translations.literal: Her father Meng served as the circuit’s memorial courier and lived in the capital; through crafty flattery he won An Chonghui’s favor and was made deputy regent of the Ye capital.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Meng was the circuit’s memorial courier in the capital; by smooth deceit he pleased An Chonghui and was made deputy regent at Ye.

sentences.zh: 高祖留守鄴都，得濛歡甚，乃為重胤娶濛女，後封吳國夫人。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was regent at Ye he took a great liking to Meng and had Chongyin marry Meng’s daughter; she was later enfeoffed Lady of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu, regent at Ye, grew fond of Meng and had Chongyin marry his daughter; later she was made Lady of Wu.

sentences.zh: 重胤早卒，后寡居，有色，出帝悅之。

translations.literal: Chongyin died young; the empress lived as a widow and was beautiful, and the Fleeing Emperor was taken with her.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin died young. The widow was beautiful, and the Fleeing Emperor desired her.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，梓宮在殯，出帝居喪中，納之以為后。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died and the imperial coffin still lay in state, the Fleeing Emperor, while in mourning, took her in and made her empress.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu had barely died—the coffin still in state—when the Fleeing Emperor, still in mourning, took her as empress.

sentences.zh: 是日，以六軍仗衛、太常鼓吹，命后至西禦莊，見於高祖影殿。

translations.literal: That day, with the Six Armies in arms and the Directorate of Ceremonies’ music, he ordered the empress to the Western Imperial Manor to be presented at Gaozu’s spirit hall.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he sent the empress, escorted by the Six Armies and imperial music, to the Western Imperial Manor to be presented at Gaozu’s spirit hall.

sentences.zh: 群臣皆賀。

translations.literal: The ministers all offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers all offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂馮道等曰：「皇太后之命，與卿等不任大慶。

translations.literal: The emperor turned to Feng Dao and the others and said: “By the empress dowager’s command, I cannot share your great rejoicing with you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Feng Dao and the rest and said: “The empress dowager’s command forbids me to share this great rejoicing with you.

sentences.zh: 」群臣出，帝與皇后酣飲歌舞，過梓宮前，酹而告曰：「皇太后之命，與先帝不任大慶。

translations.literal: ” When the ministers withdrew, the emperor and empress drank and danced in revelry; passing before the coffin he poured a libation and declared: “By the empress dowager’s command, I cannot share great rejoicing with the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: ” After the ministers left, he and the empress drank and danced. Passing the coffin he poured wine and said: “By the empress dowager’s command, I cannot rejoice with the late emperor.

sentences.zh: 」左右皆失笑，帝亦自絕倒，顧謂左右曰：「我今日作新女婿，何似？

translations.literal: ” Those beside him all lost composure and laughed; the emperor himself collapsed in mirth and, turning to his attendants, said: “How do I look as a bridegroom today?
translations.idiomatic: ” His attendants burst out laughing; the emperor himself doubled over and asked them: “How do I look as a new bridegroom today?

sentences.zh: 」后與左右皆大笑，聲聞於外。

translations.literal: ” The empress and the attendants all laughed loudly, and the sound carried outside.
translations.idiomatic: ” The empress and the attendants roared with laughter until the sound carried beyond the hall.

sentences.zh: 后既立，專內寵，封拜宮官尚宮、知客等皆為郡夫人，又用男子李彥弼為皇后宮都押衙。

translations.literal: Once enthroned, the empress held exclusive favor within; palace officers she enfeoffed as Shanggong, Guest Manager, and the like all became Ladies of Commanderies, and she even appointed the man Li Yanbi chief steward of the empress’s palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once enthroned she monopolized favor within the palace; every officer she raised—Shanggong, Guest Manager, and the rest—became a Lady of Commandery, and she even set the man Li Yanbi over the empress’s household guard.

sentences.zh: 其兄玉執政，內外用事，晉遂以亂。

translations.literal: Her elder brother Yu held power in and out of court, and Jin was thereby thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Yu ran affairs inside and outside the court, and Jin slid into chaos.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯京師，暴帝之惡於天下曰：「納叔母於中宮，亂人倫之大典。

translations.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital they broadcast the emperor’s crimes to the realm, saying: “He took his uncle’s widow into the inner palace and overturned the great canon of human relations.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took the capital they proclaimed the emperor’s crimes to the world: “He brought his uncle’s widow into the inner palace and violated the great canon of human relations.

sentences.zh: 」後隨帝北遷，哀帝之辱，數求毒藥，欲與帝俱飲以死，而藥不可得。

translations.literal: ” Later she followed the emperor north; grieving his humiliation, she repeatedly sought poison, wishing to drink it with him and die together, but no poison could be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: ” She followed him north. Grieving his disgrace, she begged again and again for poison so they might die together, but none could be found.

sentences.zh: 後不知其所終。

translations.literal: Later, what became of her is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: What became of her afterward is unknown.

sentences.zh: 高祖叔父兄弟

translations.literal: Gaozu’s paternal uncles and brothers
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s Paternal Uncles and Brothers

sentences.zh: 晉氏始出夷狄而微，終為夷狄所滅，故其宗室次序本末不能究見。

translations.literal: The Jin clan began as humble men of the barbarian borderlands and in the end was destroyed by barbarians, so the order and origins of its imperial house cannot be fully traced.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house rose from humble border barbarians and was destroyed by barbarians in the end, so the order and origins of its clan cannot be fully traced.

sentences.zh: 其可見者，曰高祖二叔父，一兄六弟，七子二孫，而有略有詳，非惟禍亂多故而失其事實，抑亦無足稱焉者。

translations.literal: What can be seen is this: Gaozu had two paternal uncles, one elder brother, six younger brothers, seven sons, and two grandsons—some noted briefly, some in detail. It is not only that turmoil and disorder caused the facts to be lost; little here is worth praising.
translations.idiomatic: What survives shows Gaozu had two paternal uncles, one elder brother, six younger brothers, seven sons, and two grandsons—some noted in passing, some at length. Facts were lost not only to war and disorder; little here merits praise.

sentences.zh: 然粗存其見者，以備其闕云。

translations.literal: Yet I roughly preserve what can be seen, to supply what is missing.
translations.idiomatic: Still, I preserve what can be seen, however roughly, to fill the gaps.

sentences.zh: 二叔父曰萬友、萬詮，兄曰敬儒，弟曰敬威、敬德、敬殷、敬赟、敬暉、重胤，子曰重貴、重信、重乂、重英、重進、重睿、重杲，孫曰延煦、延寶。

translations.literal: The two paternal uncles were Wanyou and Wanyuan; the elder brother was Jingru; the younger brothers were Jingwei, Jingde, Jingyin, Jingyun, Jinghui, and Chongyin; the sons were Chonggui, Chongxin, Chongyi, Chongying, Chongjin, Chongrui, and Chonggao; the grandsons were Yansxu and Yanbao.
translations.idiomatic: The two paternal uncles were Wanyou and Wanyuan; the elder brother, Jingru; the younger brothers Jingwei, Jingde, Jingyin, Jingyun, Jinghui, and Chongyin; the sons Chonggui, Chongxin, Chongyi, Chongying, Chongjin, Chongrui, and Chonggao; the grandsons Yansxu and Yanbao.

sentences.zh: 孝平皇帝生孝元皇帝、萬友、萬詮，孝元皇帝生高祖，萬友生敬威、敬赟，萬詮生敬暉，而敬儒、敬德、敬殷、重胤皆不知其於高祖為親疏也。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoping begot Emperor Xiaoyuan, Wanyou, and Wanyuan; Emperor Xiaoyuan begot Gaozu; Wanyou begot Jingwei and Jingyun; Wanyuan begot Jinghui; while whether Jingru, Jingde, Jingyin, and Chongyin were close or distant kin to Gaozu is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaoping fathered Emperor Xiaoyuan, Wanyou, and Wanyuan; Emperor Xiaoyuan fathered Gaozu; Wanyou fathered Jingwei and Jingyun; Wanyuan fathered Jinghui; but whether Jingru, Jingde, Jingyin, and Chongyin stood near or far from Gaozu in kinship is unknown.

sentences.zh: 高祖，孝元皇帝第二子也，而敬儒為兄，疑其長子也，則於高祖屬長而親，然贈官反最後於諸弟，而高祖世獨不得追封，此又可疑也。

translations.literal: Gaozu was Emperor Xiaoyuan’s second son, yet Jingru is called elder brother—suggesting he was the eldest son—so in relation to Gaozu he would be the senior close kin; yet posthumous offices were granted him last among the brothers, and in Gaozu’s reign alone he received no posthumous enfeoffment. This too is doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was Emperor Xiaoyuan’s second son, yet Jingru is styled elder brother—as if he were the eldest—making him Gaozu’s senior close kin; yet posthumous honors came to him last among the brothers, and under Gaozu alone he received no princely enfeoffment. That too is suspect.

sentences.zh: 重胤，高祖弟也，亦不知其為親疏，然高祖愛之，養以為子，故於名加「重」而下齒諸子。

translations.literal: Chongyin was Gaozu’s younger brother—again, whether close or distant kin is unknown—but Gaozu loved him and raised him as a son, so the name carries “Chong” and he ranks with the sons.
translations.idiomatic: Chongyin was Gaozu’s younger brother—again, near or distant kin is unclear—but Gaozu loved him, raised him as a son, gave him the “Chong” name, and ranked him with his sons.

sentences.zh: 高祖叔、兄與弟敬殷、子重進，皆前即位卒，而敬威、敬德、重胤、重英，高祖反時死。

translations.literal: Gaozu’s paternal uncles, elder brother, younger brother Jingyin, and son Chongjin all died before he took the throne; Jingwei, Jingde, Chongyin, and Chongying died when Gaozu rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s paternal uncles, elder brother, younger brother Jingyin, and son Chongjin all died before his accession; Jingwei, Jingde, Chongyin, and Chongying died when Gaozu rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高祖少子曰馮六，未名而卒，而舊說以重睿為幼子者，非也。

translations.literal: Gaozu’s youngest son was Feng Liu, who died before receiving a formal name; the old claim that Chongrui was the youngest son is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s youngest son was Feng Liu, unnamed when he died; the old story that Chongrui was the youngest is mistaken.

sentences.zh: 石氏世事軍中，萬友、萬詮職卑不見。

translations.literal: The Shi clan had long served in the army; Wanyou and Wanyuan held low posts and do not appear in the records.
translations.idiomatic: The Shi house had long served in the army; Wanyou and Wanyuan held humble posts and leave no trace in the records.

sentences.zh: 天福二年正月，萬友自故金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒兼御史大夫、上柱國贈太師。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second Tianfu year, Wanyou was posthumously promoted from former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, Concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 2, Wanyou was posthumously raised from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 萬詮亦自金紫光祿大夫、檢校司空兼御史大夫、上柱國贈太傅。

translations.literal: Wanyuan likewise was posthumously promoted from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Mentor with the Staff, Concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Wanyuan was likewise raised from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Mentor with the Staff, concurrent Grand Censor, and Pillar of the State to Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 出帝天福八年五月，追封皇叔祖萬友為秦王，萬詮加贈太師，追封趙王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth Tianfu year under the Fleeing Emperor, the imperial great-uncle Wanyou was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Qin; Wanyuan was additionally granted Grand Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 8 under the Fleeing Emperor, the imperial great-uncle Wanyou was posthumously made Prince of Qin; Wanyuan received an added grant of Grand Preceptor and was posthumously made Prince of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 從弟敬威

translations.literal: Younger cousin Jingwei
translations.idiomatic: Younger Cousin Jingwei

sentences.zh: 敬威字奉信，唐廢帝時為彰聖右第三都指揮使，領常州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingwei, styled Fengxin, was third commander of the Right Wing of the Zhangsheng Guard under Tang’s Deposed Emperor and concurrently prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwei, styled Fengxin, commanded the third division of the Right Zhangsheng Guard under Tang’s Deposed Emperor and served concurrently as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞高祖舉兵太原，謂人曰「生而有死，人孰能免？

translations.literal: When he heard that Gaozu had raised arms at Taiyuan, he told others: “Born, one must die—who can escape it?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Gaozu had risen at Taiyuan, he said: “Life ends in death—who escapes it?

sentences.zh: 吾兄方舉大事，吾不可偷生取辱，見笑一時。

translations.literal: My elder brother is undertaking a great affair; I cannot cling to life and invite disgrace, becoming a laughingstock for a season.
translations.idiomatic: My brother is attempting a great thing; I will not cling to life and invite shame, to be mocked for a season.

sentences.zh: 」遂自殺。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon he killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: ” He killed himself.

sentences.zh: 敬德時為沂州馬步軍指揮使，以高祖反誅。

translations.literal: Jingde was then commander of the cavalry and infantry of Yizhou and was executed when Gaozu rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde, then commander of Yizhou’s horse and foot, was executed when Gaozu rebelled.

sentences.zh: 天福二年正月，贈敬威、敬德皆為太傅，並贈敬殷以檢校太子賓客，亦贈太傅，而不及敬儒。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second Tianfu year, Jingwei and Jingde were both posthumously granted Grand Tutor; Jingyin was also granted Grand Tutor with the post of Acting Guest of the Heir Apparent—but Jingru was not included.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 2, Jingwei and Jingde were both posthumously made Grand Tutor; Jingyin received the same with the acting post of Guest of the Heir Apparent—but Jingru was passed over.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，追封敬威廣王，敬德福王，敬殷通王，皆贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, Jingwei was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Guang, Jingde Prince of Fu, and Jingyin Prince of Tong; all were additionally granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year, Jingwei was posthumously made Prince of Guang, Jingde Prince of Fu, and Jingyin Prince of Tong; each also received Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 敬儒始以故金紫光祿大夫、檢校尚書左僕射兼御史大夫、上柱國贈太傅，而獨不得封。

translations.literal: Jingru was first granted Grand Tutor from former Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, Concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Pillar of the State—yet alone received no enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Jingru alone was first granted Grand Tutor from Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Grand Preceptor with the Staff, concurrent Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Pillar of the State—yet received no princely title.

sentences.zh: 出帝天福八年五月，加贈三皇叔皆為太師，而皇伯敬儒始追封宋王，亦加贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth Tianfu year under the Fleeing Emperor, the three imperial uncles were all additionally granted Grand Preceptor, and the imperial elder Jingru was at last posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Song, also with additional grant of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 8 under the Fleeing Emperor, all three imperial uncles received added grants of Grand Preceptor, and the imperial elder Jingru was at last posthumously made Prince of Song, likewise raised to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 從兄敬赟

translations.literal: Older cousin Jingyun
translations.idiomatic: Older Cousin Jingyun

sentences.zh: 從弟韓王敬暉

translations.literal: Younger cousin, Prince of Han Jinghui
translations.idiomatic: Younger Cousin, Prince of Han Jinghui

sentences.zh: 韓王敬暉字德昭，為人厚重剛直，勇而多智，高祖尤愛之。

translations.literal: Prince of Han Jinghui, styled Dezhao, was grave, upright, brave, and resourceful; Gaozu loved him especially.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Han Jinghui, styled Dezhao, was steady, upright, brave, and shrewd; Gaozu loved him above the rest.

sentences.zh: 高祖時為曹州防禦使，以廉儉見稱，卒於官，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Under Gaozu he was defense commissioner of Caozhou, famed for integrity and frugality; he died in office and was granted Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozu he served as defense commissioner of Caozhou, praised for integrity and thrift; he died in office and received Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 天福八年，加贈太師，追封韓王。

translations.literal: In the eighth Tianfu year he was additionally granted Grand Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 8 he was additionally made Grand Preceptor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Han.

sentences.zh: 子曦嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xi succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 高祖諸子孫

translations.literal: Gaozu’s sons and grandsons
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s Sons and Grandsons

sentences.zh: 高祖李皇后生楚王重信，其諸子皆不知其母。

translations.literal: Empress Li of Gaozu bore Prince of Chu Chongxin; the mothers of his other sons are unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu’s Empress Li bore Prince of Chu Chongxin; the mothers of his other sons are unknown.

sentences.zh: 當高祖起太原，重英為右衛將軍，重胤為皇城副使，居京師。

translations.literal: When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Chongying was Right Guard general and Chongyin was deputy commissioner of the Imperial City; both were in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Chongying was Right Guard general and Chongyin deputy commissioner of the Imperial City—both in the capital.

sentences.zh: 聞高祖舉事，匿民家井中，捕得誅之，並族民家。

translations.literal: Hearing that Gaozu had launched his enterprise, they hid in a commoner’s well; captured, they were executed, and the commoner’s household was exterminated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the rebellion, they hid in a commoner’s well; seized, they were put to death, and the host family was exterminated.

sentences.zh: 天福二年正月，高祖為二子發哀，皆贈為太保；

translations.literal: In the first month of the second Tianfu year, Gaozu held mourning for the two sons; both were posthumously granted Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianfu 2, Gaozu mourned the two sons; both received posthumous rank as Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 並贈重進以故左金吾衛將軍贈太保。

translations.literal: Chongjin was also granted Grand Guardian from his former post as Left Golden Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Chongjin, former Left Golden Guard general, was likewise posthumously made Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，皆加贈太傅，追封重英虢王，重胤郯王，重進夔王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year all were additionally granted Grand Tutor; Chongying was posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Guo, Chongyin Prince of Tan, and Chongjin Prince of Kui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year all were raised to Grand Tutor; Chongying was posthumously made Prince of Guo, Chongyin Prince of Tan, and Chongjin Prince of Kui.

sentences.zh: 出帝天福八年五月，皆加贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth Tianfu year under the Fleeing Emperor, all were additionally granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 8 under the Fleeing Emperor, all received additional grants of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子楚王重信

translations.literal: The son, Prince of Chu Chongxin
translations.idiomatic: The Son: Prince of Chu Chongxin

sentences.zh: 楚王重信字守孚，為人敏悟多智而好禮。

translations.literal: Prince of Chu Chongxin, styled Shoufu, was quick-witted, clever, and fond of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chu Chongxin, styled Shoufu, was sharp, clever, and devoted to ritual.

sentences.zh: 天福二年二月，以左驍衛上將軍拜河陽三城節度使，有善政，高祖下詔褒之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second Tianfu year he was appointed military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang from Left Flying Cavalry senior general; his good governance won Gaozu’s edict of praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianfu 2 he was made military commissioner of the Three Cities of Heyang from senior general of the Left Flying Cavalry; Gaozu issued an edict praising his governance.

sentences.zh: 是歲範延光反，詔前靈武節度使張從賓發河陽兵討延光，從賓亦反，重信見殺，時年二十。

translations.literal: That year Fan Yanguang rebelled; an edict ordered former Lingwu military commissioner Zhang Congbin to raise Heyang troops against Yanguang. Congbin also rebelled, and Chongxin was killed—aged twenty.
translations.idiomatic: That year Fan Yanguang rebelled; the court ordered former Lingwu commissioner Zhang Congbin to march Heyang troops against him. Congbin rebelled too, and Chongxin was killed at twenty.

sentences.zh: 高祖欲贈重信太尉，大臣引漢故事，皇子無為三公者。

translations.literal: Gaozu wished to grant Chongxin Grand Commandant; the great ministers cited Han precedent that imperial sons were not made one of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu wished to grant Chongxin Grand Commandant; the chief ministers cited Han precedent: no imperial son had ever held one of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「此兒為善被禍，吾哀之甚，自我而已，豈有例邪！

translations.literal: Gaozu said: “This boy did good and met disaster; I grieve for him deeply. Let it begin with me—what need is there for precedent!
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said: “This boy did good and met calamity; my grief for him runs deep. Let the rule begin with me—what need of precedent!

sentences.zh: 」乃贈太尉。

translations.literal: ” So he was granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: ” He was granted Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，加贈太師，追封沂王。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year he was additionally granted Grand Tutor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year he was additionally made Grand Tutor and posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 出帝天福八年五月，易封楚王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth Tianfu year under the Fleeing Emperor, his enfeoffment was changed to Prince of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 8 under the Fleeing Emperor, his title was changed to Prince of Chu.

sentences.zh: 子壽王重乂

translations.literal: The son, Prince of Shou Chongyi
translations.idiomatic: The Son: Prince of Shou Chongyi

sentences.zh: 子重睿

translations.literal: The son Chongrui
translations.idiomatic: The Son Chongrui

sentences.zh: 重睿為人貌類高祖。

translations.literal: Chongrui in appearance resembled Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Chongrui resembled Gaozu in face.

sentences.zh: 高祖臥疾，宰相馮道入見臥內，重睿尚幼，高祖呼出使拜道於前，因以宦者抱持寘道懷中，高祖雖不言，左右皆知其以重睿托道也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu lay ill, Chancellor Feng Dao entered the sickroom; Chongrui was still young. Gaozu had him brought out to bow to Dao, then had a eunuch hold him and place him in Dao’s arms. Though Gaozu said nothing, all beside him knew he was entrusting Chongrui to Dao.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu lay ill when Chancellor Feng Dao came to his bedside; Chongrui was still small. Gaozu had the boy brought forward to bow to Dao, then a eunuch lifted him into Dao’s arms. Gaozu never spoke, but everyone present knew he was entrusting Chongrui to Dao.

sentences.zh: 高祖崩，晉大臣以國家多事，議立長君，而景延廣已陰許立出帝，重睿遂不得立。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died, Jin’s great ministers, finding the state beset by troubles, debated enthroning an elder prince; but Jing Yanguang had already secretly promised the throne to the Fleeing Emperor, and Chongrui was not enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: At Gaozu’s death the chief ministers, with the realm in turmoil, debated raising an elder prince; but Jing Yanguang had already secretly pledged the throne to the Fleeing Emperor, and Chongrui was passed over.

sentences.zh: 出帝以重睿為檢校太保、開封尹，以左散騎常侍邊蔚權知開封府事。

translations.literal: The Fleeing Emperor made Chongrui Acting Grand Guardian and metropolitan magistrate of Kaifeng, with Left Regular Attendant Bian Wei acting in charge of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Fleeing Emperor made Chongrui Acting Grand Guardian and prefect of Kaifeng, with Left Regular Attendant Bian Wei acting in his stead.

sentences.zh: 開運二年五月，拜重睿雄武軍節度使，歲餘，徙鎮忠武，皆不之鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second Kaiyun year he was appointed military commissioner of the Xiongwu Army; after more than a year he was transferred to the Zhongwu command, but never went to either post.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyun 2 he was named commissioner of the Xiongwu Army; a year later he was shifted to Zhongwu, but never reported to either command.

sentences.zh: 契丹滅晉，重睿從出帝北遷，後不知其所終。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Chongrui followed the Fleeing Emperor north; later, what became of him is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, Chongrui followed the Fleeing Emperor north; his fate afterward is unknown.

sentences.zh: 子重杲

translations.literal: The son Chonggao
translations.idiomatic: The Son Chonggao

sentences.zh: 陳王重杲，高祖幼子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Chonggao was Gaozu’s youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chen Chonggao was Gaozu’s youngest son.

sentences.zh: 小字馮六，未名而卒，贈太傅，追封陳王，賜名重杲。

translations.literal: His childhood name was Feng Liu; he died before receiving a formal name, was granted Grand Tutor, posthumously enfeoffed Prince of Chen, and given the name Chonggao.
translations.idiomatic: His childhood name was Feng Liu; he died unnamed, received Grand Tutor, was posthumously made Prince of Chen, and granted the name Chonggao.

sentences.zh: 出帝天福八年五月，加贈太師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth Tianfu year under the Fleeing Emperor, he was additionally granted Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Tianfu 8 under the Fleeing Emperor, he was additionally made Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 孫延煦 延寶

translations.literal: The grandsons Yansxu and Yanbao
translations.idiomatic: The Grandsons Yansxu and Yanbao

sentences.zh: 延煦、延寶，高祖諸孫也，出帝以為子。

translations.literal: Yansxu and Yanbao, grandsons of Gaozu, were taken as sons by the Fleeing Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Yansxu and Yanbao, Gaozu’s grandsons, were adopted as sons by the Fleeing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 開運二年秋，以延煦為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: In autumn of the second Kaiyun year, Yansxu was made prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn of Kaiyun 2, Yansxu was appointed prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 延煦少，不能視事，以一宦者從之，又選尚書郎路航參知州事。

translations.literal: Yansxu was young and could not administer affairs; a eunuch accompanied him, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Hang was chosen to assist in governing the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yansxu was too young to govern; a eunuch attended him, and Secretariat Gentleman Lu Hang was chosen to assist in prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 宦者遂專政事，每詬辱航，出帝召航還。

translations.literal: The eunuch then monopolized government; he repeatedly reviled and humiliated Hang, and the Fleeing Emperor recalled Hang.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch seized control of government, repeatedly reviled Hang, and the Fleeing Emperor recalled him.

sentences.zh: 已而徙延煦齊州防禦使。

translations.literal: Soon after, Yansxu was transferred to defense commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yansxu was transferred to defense commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 三年，拜鎮寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed military commissioner of the Zhenning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made military commissioner of the Zhenning Army.

sentences.zh: 是時，河北用兵，天下旱蝗，民餓死者百萬計，而諸鎮爭為聚斂，趙在禮所積鉅萬，為諸侯王最。

translations.literal: At that time the north of the Yellow River was at war; drought and locusts ravaged the realm, and starving dead numbered in the millions—yet every command fought to squeeze revenue. Zhao Zaili’s hoard ran to enormous sums, the greatest among the feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: War raged north of the Yellow River; drought and locusts scourged the land, and starvation deaths ran into the millions—yet every command squeezed revenue. Zhao Zaili’s hoard was the largest among the feudatories.

sentences.zh: 出帝利其貲，乃以延煦娶在禮女，在禮獻絹三千匹，前後所獻不可勝數。

translations.literal: The Fleeing Emperor coveted his wealth and had Yansxu marry Zaili’s daughter; Zaili presented three thousand bolts of silk, and gifts before and after were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The Fleeing Emperor coveted his wealth and married Yansxu to Zaili’s daughter; Zaili sent three thousand bolts of silk, with gifts before and after beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 三年五月，遣宗正卿石光贊以聘幣一百五十床迎於其第，出帝宴在禮萬歲殿，所以賜予甚厚，君臣窮極奢侈，時人以為榮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, Director of the Imperial Clan Shi Guangzan was sent with betrothal gifts of one hundred fifty beds to fetch her from Zaili’s residence; the Fleeing Emperor feasted Zaili in the Hall of Ten Thousand Years, lavishing gifts so richly that lord and subject exhausted extravagance—men of the time took it for glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the third year, Imperial Clan Director Shi Guangzan went with one hundred fifty beds of betrothal gifts to fetch the bride from Zaili’s house; the Fleeing Emperor feasted him in the Hall of Ten Thousand Years with gifts so lavish that ruler and subject outdid each other in excess—contemporaries called it glory.

sentences.zh: 在禮謂人曰：「吾此一婚，其費十萬。

translations.literal: Zaili told others: “This one marriage of mine cost a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zaili told others: “This marriage cost me a hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 」十一月，徙延煦鎮保義。

translations.literal: ” In the eleventh month Yansxu was transferred to command the Baoyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: ” In the eleventh month Yansxu was transferred to the Baoyi command.

sentences.zh: 自延煦為齊州防禦使，而延寶代為鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: From the time Yansxu became defense commissioner of Qizhou, Yanbao replaced him as prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yansxu took Qizhou, Yanbao replaced him as prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 及契丹滅晉，出帝與太后遣延煦、延寶賫降表、玉璽、金印以歸契丹，而延寶時亦為威信軍節度使矣。

translations.literal: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, the Fleeing Emperor and the empress dowager sent Yansxu and Yanbao bearing the surrender memorial, jade seal, and gold seal to the Khitan; by then Yanbao was also military commissioner of the Weixin Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan destroyed Jin, the Fleeing Emperor and empress dowager sent Yansxu and Yanbao with the surrender memorial, jade seal, and gold seal to the Khitan; Yanbao was by then commissioner of the Weixin Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹得璽，以為制作非工，與前史所傳者異，命延煦等還報求真璽。

translations.literal: The Khitan received the seal and judged the workmanship inferior, unlike seals recorded in earlier histories; they ordered Yansxu and the others to return and report, demanding the true seal.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan took the seal, found the workmanship poor and unlike seals in earlier histories, and sent Yansxu back to demand the true one.

sentences.zh: 出帝以狀答曰：「頃潞王從珂自焚於洛陽，玉璽不知所在，疑已焚之。

translations.literal: The Fleeing Emperor replied in a memorial: “When the Prince of Lu, Congke, burned himself at Luoyang, the jade seal’s whereabouts were unknown—it is thought to have been destroyed in the fire.
translations.idiomatic: The Fleeing Emperor answered: “When Prince of Lu Congke burned himself at Luoyang, the jade seal vanished—it was likely destroyed in the fire.

sentences.zh: 先帝受命，命玉工制此璽，在位群臣皆知之。

translations.literal: When the late emperor received the Mandate, he ordered jade craftsmen to make this seal; the ministers in office at the time all know it.
translations.idiomatic: When the late emperor received the Mandate he had craftsmen fashion this seal; every minister then in office knows it.

sentences.zh: 」乃已。

translations.literal: ” And there the matter rested.
translations.idiomatic: ” And there the matter ended.

sentences.zh: 後延煦等從出帝北遷，不知其所終。

translations.literal: Later Yansxu and the others followed the Fleeing Emperor north; what became of them is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yansxu and the others followed the Fleeing Emperor north; their fate is unknown.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 古之不幸無子，而以其同宗之子為後者，聖人許之，著之《禮》經而不諱也。

translations.literal: In antiquity, when men were unhappily without sons and took a son of the same clan as heir, the sages permitted it and recorded it in the Book of Rites without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, when a man had no son and took a kinsman’s child as heir, the sages permitted it and set it down openly in the Book of Rites.

sentences.zh: 而後世閭閻鄙俚之人則諱之，諱則不勝其欺與偽也。

translations.literal: Later generations of common folk in lane and hamlet hide it; and in hiding it they cannot escape deceit and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations of common folk hide the matter; and hiding it, they cannot escape fraud and pretense.

sentences.zh: 故其茍偷竊取嬰孩繈褓，諱其父母，而自欺以為我生之子，曰：「不如此，則不能得其一誌盡愛於我，而其心必二也。

translations.literal: So they furtively steal an infant in swaddling clothes, hide its parents, and fool themselves into thinking it their own child, saying: “If I do not do this, I cannot win its whole heart’s love for me—and its heart would surely be divided.
translations.idiomatic: So they furtively seize an infant in swaddling clothes, conceal its parents, and persuade themselves it is their own, saying: “Otherwise I cannot win its whole heart—and its heart would be divided.

sentences.zh: 」而為其子者，亦自諱其所生，而絕其天性之親，反視以為叔伯父，以此欺其九族，而亂其人鬼親疏之屬。

translations.literal: ” And the child, too, hides its birth and severs natural kinship, instead treating its natural parents as uncles and aunts, thus deceiving the nine agnates and confounding the ranks of kin among the living and the dead.
translations.idiomatic: ” The child, too, hides its birth and cuts natural ties, treating its own parents as uncles and aunts, deceiving the nine agnates and confounding kinship among the living and the dead.

sentences.zh: 凡物生而有知，未有不愛其父母者。

translations.literal: All things born with consciousness love their parents—none do not.
translations.idiomatic: Every living thing that knows loves its parents—none fails to.

sentences.zh: 使是子也，能忍而真絕其天性歟，曾禽獸之不若也。

translations.literal: If such a son could endure and truly sever his nature, he would be worse than birds and beasts.
translations.idiomatic: If such a son could truly endure and kill natural feeling, he would fall below birds and beasts.

sentences.zh: 使其不忍而外陽絕之，是大偽也。

translations.literal: If he cannot endure yet outwardly pretends severance, that is great falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot endure yet outwardly feigns severance, that is the deepest fraud.

sentences.zh: 夫閭閻鄙俚之人之慮於事者，亦已深矣！

translations.literal: The common folk’s calculation in such matters runs very deep indeed!
translations.idiomatic: Common folk calculate such matters very deeply indeed!

sentences.zh: 然而茍竊欺偽不可以為法者，小人之事也。

translations.literal: Yet furtive theft and deceit cannot serve as law—that is the way of petty men.
translations.idiomatic: Yet furtive fraud cannot be law—that is the petty man’s way.

sentences.zh: 惟聖人則不然，以謂人道莫大於繼絕，此萬世之通制而天下之公行也，何必諱哉！

translations.literal: The sages are not so. They hold that nothing in human relations exceeds continuing a severed line—this is the universal rule for ten thousand generations and the public practice under Heaven. Why must it be hidden!
translations.idiomatic: The sages are otherwise. They hold that no human duty exceeds continuing a severed line—the universal rule for all ages and the open practice of the world. Why hide it!

sentences.zh: 所謂子者，未有不由父母而生者也，故為人後者，必有所生之父，有所後之父，此理之自然也，何必諱哉！

translations.literal: What is called a son is never born except of parents; therefore one who becomes another’s heir must have the father who begot him and the father he succeeds—this is the natural order of reason. Why must it be hidden!
translations.idiomatic: A son is never born except of parents; one who becomes another’s heir must have both a natural father and a successor father—that is reason’s natural order. Why hide it!

sentences.zh: 其簡易明白，不茍不竊，不欺不偽，可以為通制而公行者，聖人之法也。

translations.literal: What is plain and simple, neither furtive nor stolen, neither deceiving nor false, and can serve as universal rule and public practice—that is the sages’ law.
translations.idiomatic: What is plain and simple—neither furtive nor stolen, neither deceitful nor false—and can serve as universal rule and public practice: that is the sages’ law.

sentences.zh: 又以謂為人之後者所承重，故加其服以斬。

translations.literal: They also hold that one who becomes another’s heir bears the weight of succession, and so his mourning garments are raised to the highest grade of hemp.
translations.idiomatic: They also hold that one who becomes another’s heir bears the weight of succession, and so his mourning is raised to the highest grade of hemp.

sentences.zh: 而不絕其所生之親者，天性之不可絕也，然而恩有屈於義，故降其服以期。

translations.literal: Yet not severing kinship with those who begot him is because natural affection cannot be severed; still, where affection yields to duty, the mourning grade is lowered to the one-year term.
translations.idiomatic: Not severing the natural tie is because affection cannot be killed; yet where affection yields to duty, mourning is lowered to the one-year grade.

sentences.zh: 服，外物也，可以降，而父母之名不可改，故著於經曰：「為人後者，為其父母報。

translations.literal: Garments are external things and may be lowered; but a parent’s name cannot be changed, so the classic records: “One who becomes another’s heir still performs mourning for his natural parents.
translations.idiomatic: Garments are outward and may be lowered; but a parent’s name cannot be changed, so the classic says: “One who becomes another’s heir still mourns his natural parents.

sentences.zh: 」自三代以來，有天下國家者莫不用之，而晉氏不用也。

translations.literal: ” Since the Three Dynasties, none who held realm or state has failed to use this—yet the Jin clan did not.
translations.idiomatic: ” Since the Three Dynasties, every ruler of realm or state has followed this—yet the Jin house did not.

sentences.zh: 出帝之於敬儒，絕其父道，臣而爵之，非特以其義不當立，不得已而絕之，蓋亦習見閭閻鄙俚之所為也。

translations.literal: The Fleeing Emperor toward Jingru severed the way of fatherhood, made him a subject and ennobled him—not only because his enthronement was illegitimate and severance was unavoidable, but also because he was accustomed to what common folk in lane and hamlet do.
translations.idiomatic: The Fleeing Emperor toward Jingru severed the way of fatherhood, ennobled the man who begot him and styled himself that man’s subject—not only because his accession was illegitimate and severance seemed unavoidable, but because he had grown used to the ways of common folk.

sentences.zh: 五代，干戈賊亂之世也，禮樂崩壞，三綱五常之道絕，而先王之制度文章掃地而盡於是矣！

translations.literal: The Five Dynasties were an age of arms, rebellion, and disorder; ritual and music collapsed, the way of the Three Bonds and Five Constants was cut off, and the former kings’ institutions and writings were swept clean at last!
translations.idiomatic: The Five Dynasties were an age of war, rebellion, and chaos; ritual and music collapsed, the Three Bonds and Five Constants were severed, and the institutions and writings of the former kings were swept away!

sentences.zh: 如寒食野祭而焚紙錢，天子而為閭閻鄙俚之事者多矣！

translations.literal: Cold Food sacrifices in the open wild and the burning of paper money—how many emperors performed the petty customs of lane and hamlet!
translations.idiomatic: Cold Food rites in the open wild, spirit money burned—how many emperors practiced the petty customs of common folk!

sentences.zh: 而晉氏起於夷狄，以篡逆而得天下，高祖以耶律德光為父，而出帝於德光則以為祖而稱孫，於其所生父則臣而名之，是豈可以人理責哉！

translations.literal: Yet the Jin clan rose from barbarians, seized the realm by usurpation and rebellion; Gaozu took Yelü Deguang as father, and the Fleeing Emperor treated Deguang as grandfather and styled himself grandson, while toward the father who begot him he made a subject and addressed him by name—how can such men be judged by human reason!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Jin house rose from barbarians and won the realm by usurpation; Gaozu called Yelü Deguang father, and the Fleeing Emperor called Deguang grandfather and styled himself grandson, while toward his own father he made a subject and spoke his name—how can human reason be asked of such men!
